placement_rule.unit: position = bottom-centre of the nominal box in prefab space; rotation_euler_deg is the unit rotation (all 0). The box is only nominal: settled copies lie where physics put them and may leave it; the crate cavity is the real container.
placement_rule.copy: SETTLED transform, in unit-local space. Scale the item's own model uniformly so its renderer bounds, after the alignment, fit inside fit_box (contain-fit; fit_box IS the aligned scaled bounds, so the scale is exact; it differs per crate, mass storage keeps the layouts' own item sizes). align 'up' = item as it comes; align 'long_x' = first rotate the item so its longest bounds axis lies along the unit's width axis (item +long axis -> Blender +x = Unity -x). Then rotate by rot_euler_deg about the bounds centre. anchor 'center': the bounds centre (leaves included) of the (aligned, unrotated) scaled item sits at offset, then the rotation applies about that centre. Copies are listed in drop order (order).
placement_rule.fill: units are listed in fill order, crate by crate. Crate-wise fill: a crate holding n stacks shows its first n units (slot_in_crate 0..7); global fill: the first round(f * slots) units. One unit = one full stack of one item type. Stack k was dropped onto stacks 0..k-1 after those were frozen, so adding stacks never moves earlier ones.
placement_rule.classes: a crate has one class (pile / bundle / sheaf / row): put an item in a crate of its shape class (round or leafy, long, tied plant, cap).

physics.method: Blender rigid body (Bullet): crate floor and walls = passive boxes, items = active convex hulls of the item BODY only (alpha-clipped leaf material excluded; leaves ride along with no collision), friction 0.8, restitution 0, damping 0.50/0.95, margin 1.5 mm, substeps 20, solver iterations 40; one stack's copy per crate settled and frozen before the next. A try is rejected and re-dropped if a body is farther than 5 mm from its support (floor or an earlier body below), or any vertex (leaves included) leaves the cavity (leaves may sink into the floor).

crop_layouts_doc: crop_layouts: one physics-settled full crate per crop (item prefab name; '_generic' for any other item, the eggs included). A crate holding n stacks of an item shows stacks[0..n-1] of that item's layout (all of a stack's copies), so filling never moves earlier copies. Round 8b: every crop at round 7's scale (no shrinking); each crate was filled as one drop sequence until it refused copies, and that sequence was cut into 8 consecutive stacks, floor-weighted: stacks 0..2 hold the floor layer (so 3 stacks cover the floor), stacks 3..7 the heap above it, no stack over the runtime's 6000-triangle stack cap. Any consecutive cut keeps every prefix supported. Round 8: FLOOR FIRST. Every copy was dropped at the lowest free spot of the crate, ties broken by distance to the copies already there (and to the walls), so stack 0 spreads over the whole floor (all four quadrants), later copies fill the gaps, then the heap builds up layer by layer and slopes up from the front lip; no half, no divider. Copies are listed in drop order inside each stack, and every copy rests on the floor, a wall or a copy listed before it (earlier stack, or earlier in its own stack), so any prefix (n stacks, and a partial last stack) is supported. Per copy: start from the item's model in the mod's item space (ItemVisual: prefab root space without the root's own scale, turned 180 degrees about up, exactly as round 4), scale it uniformly by 'scale' (= x the item's true size; RootScale NOT applied), rotate it by rot_quat_xyzw about its bounds centre (the WHOLE item's bounds, greens included), and put that bounds centre at crate_floor_centres[crate] + offset (prefab space, Unity y-up/+z front; offset is crate-floor-centre local, the store's unit rotation is identity). Carrot and Turnip were settled and checked without their greens (the mod draws them Topless); their greens may overlap anything. The layouts were settled in one generic cavity (0.53 wide x 0.45 deep x 0.424 high above the floor centre, the lowest common crate) with colliders only as high as the real boards (front lip 0.103, sides 0.233, back 0.415 over the floor centre) and checked in all nine crates. '_generic' has scale null: scale the item so its longest bounds side is fit_longest_m. Copies per stack x the item's triangles stays under the runtime's 6000-triangle stack cap. Per crop also: true_size_m (bounds at scale 1, Unity x,y,z), mode, copies_per_stack, check (copies, dropped, float_worst_mm, clipping_in_9_crates, interpen_max_mm, heap_top_m and fill_mean_m above the floor centre, fill_cover, floor_first: stack 0's floor cover and quadrant counts, cover and mean heap height by stacks 1..8; triangles). crate_floor_centres = crates[].floor_centre, by crate index. units[] (round 4, per-crate example items) are kept for the current mod.

crop_layouts_scale_exceptions.rule: round 8b: every crop at round 7's scale, unchanged (fit_longest_m too for _generic).

physics_r8: Blender rigid body (Bullet), round 6's settings: items = active convex hulls (carrot, turnip: the root alone; barley, flax, thistle, dandelion, fiddlehead: a core, the hull pulled in {'Barley': 0.8, 'Flax': 0.8, 'Thistle': 0.55, 'Dandelion': 0.6, 'Fiddleheadfern': 0.8}), friction 0.8, restitution 0, damping 0.50/0.95, margin 1.5 mm, substeps 20, iterations 40; up to 4 copies of a crop per batch at separate spots, settled then frozen. Colliders: floor, front lip, side boards and back only as high as the real boards. A spot is the lowest free one (ties: farthest from the copies already in the crate and from the walls x2), under a 35 degree slope up from the lip and the side boards. A try is re-dropped when a body is farther than 5 mm from a support frozen before it or a drawn vertex leaves the crate's column (leaves may sink 60 mm into the floor, core crops 30 mm). Each crop its own seed (8 + crop name).
